summary: Plan resilient urban water, wastewater, and flood investments with practical risk, mapping, and financing tools. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Climate-resilient urban water planning helps planners, utility managers, engineers and adaptation teams assess risks to essential services and plan investments. Participants learn to map climate hazards and infrastructure exposure, assess vulnerabilities across water supply, wastewater, sanitation and flood services, and record priorities in risk registers. They also compare options using life-cycle costs and investment appraisal, then shape findings into an implementation roadmap with indicators and responsibilities.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals coordinating climate-resilient urban water, wastewater, sanitation, and flood investments across planning, utility, engineering, and programme teams.
prerequisites: Prior experience in urban planning, water or wastewater services, infrastructure projects, environmental engineering, or climate adaptation is recommended. No coding is required. Bring a laptop with Excel and QGIS available for guided mapping and appraisal exercises; QGIS is free and open-source, while Excel may require a commercial licence.
